scenario: AITA for making a Facebook post about someone without telling them? | My (22F) best friend (21M) recently went on a 3 month long trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped to build a water pipeline and taught kids in a local school about hygiene and sanitation. He also paid for the whole trip himself, costing over $3000. He is a pretty shy and quiet guy, so he didn’t tell many people about it before he left and I doubt he was going to when he got back if I didn’t do this. I thought that he needed recognition for the great work he was doing, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to tell all of his friends and family who he hadn’t told about this trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was he didn’t have any internet connection, so he didn’t see my post until he started travelling home. When he got home I couldn’t wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport, but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn’t want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn’t want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he’s such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self improvement, not to help volunteer, he felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn’t want the attention of that post, and I shouldn’t of made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn’t see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him, I didn’t say anything bad. AITA for making that post?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by making that Facebook post about my best friend's trip to India. Let me start by going through the situation again to make sure I understand all the details. My best friend, who's 21, went on a three-month trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped build a water pipeline and taught kids in a local school about hygiene and sanitation. That's pretty impressive! Plus, he paid for the entire trip himself, which cost over $3000. He's a pretty shy and quiet guy, so I don't think he told many people about it before he left. I even doubt he would have told people when he got back if I hadn't done this. I thought he needed recognition for the great work he was doing, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to tell all his friends and family who he hadn't told about the trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was, he didn't have any internet connection, so he didn't see my post until he started traveling home. When he got home, I couldn't wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn't want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn't want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he's such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self-improvement, not to help volunteer. He felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all his friends and family about it. He said he didn't want the attention of that post, and I shouldn't have made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn't see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was doing a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him; I didn't say anything bad. So, the question is: Did I do the right thing by making that Facebook post? Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Ass) for making that post? Alright, let's break this down. First, I need to understand the key points of the situation: 1. My friend went on a volunteer trip to India, which is a significant and commendable effort. 2. He paid for the entire trip himself, which is a big financial commitment. 3. He's shy and quiet, so he likely wouldn't share this information with others on his own. 4. I made a Facebook post about his trip to give him recognition. 5. He didn't have internet access while he was away, so he didn't see the post until he started traveling home. 6. When he got home, he seemed annoyed with me, and later he expressed that he didn't want any attention for his trip, didn't want people thinking he was bragging, and that his main reason for going was for self-improvement, not just to volunteer. 7. He felt that my post was unnecessary and that I shouldn't have done it without asking him, especially since he wouldn't see it for another week. 8. I was annoyed because I thought I was doing something nice by giving him recognition, especially since he's shy and wouldn't do it himself. Now, to determine whether I did the right thing, I need to consider several factors: - **Respect for Privacy**: Did I respect my friend's privacy by sharing information about his trip without his consent? - **Intentions**: Were my intentions to help him by giving him recognition, or did I have other motives? - **Impact on the Relationship**: How did this action affect our relationship? Did it cause tension or hurt feelings? - **Understanding His Perspective**: Did I take the time to understand why he didn't want the attention, or did I assume I knew what was best for him? - **Communication**: Did I communicate with him before making the post, or did I act without discussing it with him? Let's explore each of these factors in more detail. **1. Respect for Privacy** When I made the Facebook post about my friend's trip, I shared personal information about him without his consent. Even though I had good intentions, sharing someone's personal experiences without their permission can be seen as an invasion of privacy. My friend is shy and quiet, which might mean he values his privacy more than others. By posting about his trip, I took away his control over how and when his story is shared. **2. Intentions** My intention was to give my friend recognition for his volunteer work because I thought he deserved it. I also wanted to highlight his selflessness and the positive impact he had on the community in India. However, I assumed that he would want this recognition. I didn't consider that he might prefer to keep his experiences private or that he might not want attention for his actions. **3. He later expressed that he was upset about the post, which led to tension between us. This shows that my action had a negative impact on our relationship, at least in the short term. **4. Understanding His Perspective** I didn't take the time to understand why my friend didn't want the attention. I assumed that because I thought it was a good thing, he would feel the same way. However, his reasons for going on the trip were more about self-improvement than about volunteering, and he didn't want people to think he was bragging. I didn't consider his perspective and his reasons for not wanting attention. **5. Communication** I didn't communicate with my friend before making the post. I acted on my own without discussing it with him. This lack of communication led to misunderstandings and hurt feelings. If I had talked to him about making the post, I might have understood his perspective and made a decision that respected his wishes. **Conclusion** Based on these factors, it seems that making the Facebook post without my friend's consent was not the right thing to do. While my intentions were good, I didn't respect his privacy, I didn't understand his perspective, and I didn't communicate with him before taking action. These factors led to tension and hurt feelings in our relationship. However, it's also important to consider that my friend might have been more understanding if I had communicated with him beforehand. If I had talked to him about making the post, explained my intentions, and listened to his concerns, we might have reached a mutual understanding. In the future, it would be better to communicate with my friend before sharing personal information about him. This way, I can respect his privacy, understand his perspective, and make decisions that are considerate of both of our feelings. Additionally, it's important to reflect on why I felt the need to give him recognition. While it's good to acknowledge and appreciate others' efforts, it's also important to respect their boundaries and preferences. Not everyone wants their personal achievements to be publicly recognized, and it's important to honor that.
